newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Winbond mulls huge wafer project.
newsitem.headline: Winbond mulls huge wafer project.

text.p: Winbond Electronics Corp, one of Taiwan's leading chipmakers, said on Thursday it was considering investing in a huge wafer project in the island's burgeoning southern Tainan science park over a 10-year span.

"Foreseeing the rising demand, we are considering a huge wafer project in the Tainan science park, but we have yet to make the final decision," a Winbond spokesman and assistant manager Mike Liu told Reuters by telephone.
The local Commercial Times newspaper said on Thursday Winbond will invest T$160 billion in the next 10 years to build one eight-inch and two 12-inch wafer plants in Tainan.
"We cannot confirm the figure now, but once we make the final decision, the investment amount will be around that level (of T$160 billion)," Liu said.
The announcement came after two leading chipmakers' huge investment plans and one relatively smaller plan recently.
Last week, United Microelectronics announced plans to invest T$500 billion in a wafer fabrication project, raising the stakes in the island's integrated circuits war
The project, Taiwan's single biggest investment scheme to date, called for the completion of six advanced eight-inch and 12-inch fabrication plants in the Tainnan science park over a 10 years.
In April, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, said it would launch a T$400 billion wafer project in the same science park.

Taiwan's Powerchip Co, a joint venture between the Umax-Elite group and Mitsubishi Electric, said on Wednesday it planned to invest a further T$38 billion in its planned second memory-chip plant in Taiwan.
The firm said in a statement the extra funding would enable it to equip the new plant to make advanced 12-inch dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) wafers as well as eight-inch DRAM wafers.
